title: Expose independent Cartesian damping controls
goal: Make Release Franky Cartesian translational and rotational damping explicit, independently configurable, passed to the Franky 2.x tracker, documented, and covered by focused no-hardware tests.
doneWhen: Cartesian compliance accepts optional translational_damping and rotational_damping values with clear backward-compatible behavior.
Franky passes an explicit six-axis damping vector whenever either damping value is configured, using critical damping only for omitted axes.
The Release Franka/Pico configuration declares all four Cartesian impedance fields: translational stiffness/damping and rotational stiffness/damping.
Focused tests prove damping-vector construction and configuration parsing; no hardware is started.
decisions: A missing damping value retains critical damping for that axis rather than silently becoming zero.
The Release configuration explicitly provides both translational and rotational damping so all four requested parameters are visible and effective.
This changes controller behavior and requires a new operator-led unloaded, small-range hardware validation before any stability claim.

verification.summary: Release commit 0990ae9 makes both Cartesian damping components independently configurable and declares all four Cartesian impedance fields in the Release configuration.
checks: Configuration parse verified translational stiffness/damping and rotational stiffness/damping
Python compilation and shell syntax checks passed
limitations: No hardware was exercised after changing the explicit translational damping path.
The configured translational damping retains the prior critical value (2*sqrt(1200)); changing it later is a new safety-sensitive control experiment requiring operator authorization and revalidation.
